comments.title: Electric Service Planning Application Not Submitted to Austin Energy
comments.comment: No Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) form has been submitted to Austin Energy to initiate electric service design for this 39-unit townhome development.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires ESPA submission to Austin Energy before electric service design begins; AE Design holds exclusive authority to determine service characteristics including transformer sizing and service routing. The ESPA form is absent from the submittal package — while AE's completeness check is noted as complete in the Master Comment Report and Sheet 21 shows preliminary electrical design, neither confirms that a formal ESPA was filed. The following required ESPA content items are also unverified:
- Point-of-service location (must be AE-determined, not applicant self-determined)
- Projected electrical load / demand calculations for 39 units
- Estimated service date (month/year or season)
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Master Comment Report – Electric Review
comments.resolution: Submit a completed ESPA form to Austin Energy including: (1) point-of-service location, (2) projected electrical load/demand calculations for all 39 units, (3) estimated service date, and (4) any applicable case number and address verification. Provide a copy of the submitted ESPA and Austin Energy's written acknowledgment or acceptance letter with the plan resubmittal.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Resolution requires coordination with Austin Energy (AE Design) to initiate and complete the ESPA process; AE holds determination authority over service characteristics.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Sub-items for point-of-service location, projected load, and estimated service date were each flagged in only 1/3 runs — verify each is present in the ESPA when submitted.

perRunFindings.comment: Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) form submission to Austin Energy not verified in submitted documentation. Provide evidence of ESPA submission to AE or confirm whether a service-only determination has been made that waives the ESPA requirement.

Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) form submittal to Austin Energy not confirmed. While Austin Energy completeness check shows 'complete,' the actual ESPA form is not available in supplementary documentation submitted. Provide copy of ESPA form and Austin Energy acceptance letter confirming service requirements determination.

Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) form has not been submitted to Austin Energy to initiate the electric service design process and determine transformer and service requirements for the 39-unit townhome development. Submit completed ESPA form with point-of-service location, projected electrical load, case number (if applicable), address verification (if applicable), and estimated service date.
Point-of-service location not provided with ESPA form. Include point-of-service location in the completed ESPA submitted to Austin Energy.

Projected electrical load not provided with ESPA form. Include electrical demand calculations and load projections in the ESPA submitted to Austin Energy, incorporating anticipated residential electrical demand for 39 units.
Estimated service date not provided with ESPA form. Include estimated service date (month/year or season) in the ESPA submitted to Austin Energy.

comments.title: Separate ESPA Required for Each of Eight Buildings
comments.comment: No separate ESPA form has been submitted for each of the eight individual buildings in this multi-building development as required by UCM § 1.4.2.6.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires a separate ESPA — with building number identified — for each building in a multi-building project so that AE Design can evaluate individual transformer and service requirements per structure. The site plan shows eight distinct buildings (Buildings 1–8, totaling 39 townhome units of varying configuration) but no per-building ESPA submissions are present in the application package.
comments.applicableArea: Buildings 1 through 8 – individual electric service points
comments.resolution: Submit a separate ESPA form for each of the eight buildings (Buildings 1–8), with the building number clearly identified on each form. Coordinate with Austin Energy Design to confirm per-building service and transformer requirements.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Requires coordination with Austin Energy Design to process per-building ESPA submissions.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — verify whether UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires per-building ESPAs for this project type or whether a single project-wide ESPA is permissible.

perRunFindings.comment: Separate ESPA not submitted for each building in the 8-building project with building number included. Submit individual ESPA forms for each of the 8 buildings (Buildings 1 through 8) with building numbers clearly identified.

comments.title: Design Intake Form Not Submitted Through Austin Energy AB+C Portal
comments.comment: No Design Intake Form has been submitted to Austin Energy through the AB+C portal to initiate formal electric design coordination for this project.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires a Design Intake Form submission through the AB+C portal for projects requiring AE Design coordination, including those with facility modifications, pole relocations, transmission line clearance constraints, or new service to buildings increasing load. This project has documented transmission line crossing requirements (Sheet 3, General Notes Block 20 identifies a required safety meeting with AE contact Andrew Perez, 512-505-7153) and proposes new service to 39 units — both conditions that trigger the Design Intake Form requirement. No such form is present in the submitted documentation.
comments.sheets: General Notes (Sheet 3); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Master Comment Report – Electric Review
comments.applicableArea: Austin Energy design coordination – transmission line clearance and new service for entire site
comments.resolution: Submit the Design Intake Form to Austin Energy through the AB+C portal for coordination of: (1) transmission line clearances and constraints, (2) facility modifications, and (3) new electric service for all 39 units across 8 buildings. Provide confirmation of submission and any AE Design response with the plan resubmittal.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Requires submission to and processing by Austin Energy Design through the AB+C portal.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Medium confidence (2/3 runs) — verify whether AE completeness check documentation in the Master Comment Report satisfies or substitutes for the Design Intake Form requirement.

perRunFindings.comment: Design Intake Form not confirmed submitted to Austin Energy through AB+C portal. While transmission line coordination is documented on Sheet 3, no Design Intake Form is present in supplementary documents. Submit Design Intake Form confirmation and receipt from Austin Energy AB+C portal showing design process initiation for infrastructure coordination.
applicableAreas: Electric design coordination with Austin Energy Design

perRunFindings.comment: Design Intake Form not submitted to Austin Energy through AB+C portal to initiate electric design process. Submit Design Intake Form for design coordination required for facility modifications, transmission line clearances, and infrastructure interactions.

comments.title: Underground Electric Routing Absent from Site Plan and Landscape Plan
comments.comment: Underground electric cabling routing and conduit locations are shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) but are not depicted on the Site Plan (Sheet 9), Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), or Utility Tap Plan (Sheet 19) as required.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B requires underground electric cabling routing and conduit locations to be shown on the site plan depicting all utilities, the landscape plan, and all electrical plans. Sheet 9 shows other underground utilities (water, wastewater, storm drain) in detail but omits all underground electric routing, showing only a single transformer pad. Sheet 31 shows existing overhead electric (OHE) on the boundary but no underground conduit or service lines. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) includes a legend entry for 'Proposed Underground Electric (–E–)' but draws no such lines anywhere on the plan. The complete underground routing from the Valley View Road connection through pull boxes to transformer pads and meters is documented only on Sheet 21.
comments.sheets: Site Plan – All Utilities (Sheet 9); Utility Tap Plan (Sheet 19); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: Entire site – underground electric distribution from Valley View Road connection through pull boxes to transformer pads and building meters
comments.resolution: Add underground electric line routing (using the –E– designation) to Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan), showing conduit paths from the property line source through all pull box locations to each transformer pad and service connection point, consistent with the routing shown on Sheet 21. On Sheet 19, draw the underground electric lines that are currently defined only in the legend.

perRunFindings.comment: Underground electric cabling routing is shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) but is missing or incomplete on other required plan sheets. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) contains legend symbols for underground electric but these symbols are not actually used in the drawing area. Underground electric routing must be consistently shown on the site plan showing all utilities (Sheet 9), landscape plan (Sheet 31), and utility plans (Sheet 19) per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B.

Underground electric cabling routing and conduit locations are not shown on Site Plan (Sheet 9) or Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), despite these being required 'all utilities' plan sheets per UCM § 1.4.2.6. Add underground electric line routing, conduit paths, and service connections to both sheets showing how power is distributed from the source (Valley View Road connection) to the transformer pads and to building meters.

Underground electric conduit routing and service lines must be shown on all required plan sheets including site plan showing all utilities (Sheet 9) and landscape plan (Sheet 31). Add underground electric line routing showing connections from property line source through site to service connection points per UCM § 1.4.2.6.

comments.title: Transformer Pad Locations Inconsistent and Missing Across Required Sheets
comments.comment: Transformer pad locations shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) are not consistently reproduced on the Site Plan (Sheet 9) or Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), and the number of transformers shown varies between sheets.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B requires transformer locations to be shown on the site plan depicting all utilities, the landscape plan, and all electrical plans. Sheet 21 shows either two or five transformer pads (runs varied: two in the western/eastern areas per run-1; five labeled pads near Buildings 1, 2, 4, 7, and 8 per run-3). Sheet 9 shows only one transformer pad labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' on the western side near Building 1/2, omitting all others. Sheet 31 shows no transformer pads at all. The discrepancy prevents confirmation that landscape design has coordinated around electrical equipment placement and introduces ambiguity about the actual transformer count.
comments.sheets: Site Plan – All Utilities (Sheet 9); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: Entire site – transformer pad locations near Buildings 1, 2, 4, 7, and 8
comments.resolution: Reconcile the transformer count across sheets: confirm the total number of transformer pads on Sheet 21, then add all transformer pad symbols with labels to Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) to match Sheet 21. Resolve the discrepancy between the single 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' notation on Sheet 9 and the multiple pads shown on Sheet 21.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Runs disagreed on total transformer count (2 vs. 5 pads on Sheet 21) — reviewer should verify the correct number from Sheet 21 directly.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer pads are shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) with two pads identified, but the Site Plan showing all utilities (Sheet 9) shows only one transformer pad, and the Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) shows none. Transformer locations must be clearly shown on all required plan sheets per UCM § 1.4.2.6. Clarify the number and location of transformers and ensure they are depicted on the site plan showing all utilities, landscape plan, and all electrical plans.

Transformer pad locations are not shown on Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), despite this being a required plan sheet per UCM § 1.4.2.6. Add transformer pad symbols and labels to Sheet 31 matching those shown on Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) to ensure complete infrastructure coordination across all utility plan sheets.

Transformer pad locations must be shown on the landscape plan (Sheet 31) and site plan showing all utilities (Sheet 9). Show all transformer pad locations with corresponding labels to ensure proper coordination with landscape design and site layout per UCM § 1.4.2.6.

comments.title: One-Line Electrical Riser Diagram and Secondary Riser Configuration Missing
comments.comment: No one-line diagram of the electrical riser or secondary riser configuration has been included in the plan set for this 39-unit development.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B explicitly requires a One-Line Diagram of the electrical riser as a mandatory plan sheet for all sites, and also requires the secondary riser configuration to be shown on electrical plans. Neither document is present: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) provides only a plan-view site layout of transformer locations, pull boxes, meters, and underground routing — it contains no schematic one-line diagram and no reference to one on another sheet. No other sheet in the 39-sheet plan set and no supplementary document contains this diagram. Without it, AE Design cannot verify service architecture, voltage/amperage ratings, main disconnect sizing, or distribution panel configuration from the transformer pads to individual unit meters.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) – diagram absent from this sheet and all others
comments.applicableArea: Electrical design documentation – entire site, service from AE transformers through secondary system to all 39 units
comments.resolution: Provide a complete One-Line (Single-Line) Diagram of the electrical riser as a separate plan sheet. The diagram must show: service entrance from Austin Energy, voltage and phase configuration, main service disconnect with amperage rating, distribution panel(s), branch circuit protective devices, load distribution per building, and how secondary electric service is routed from each transformer pad to individual building units. Include the secondary riser configuration showing distribution to each of the 8 buildings.

perRunFindings.comment: One-Line Diagram of the electrical riser is not included in the plan set. UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B requires this diagram as a required plan sheet. Provide a complete One-Line Diagram showing the electrical system architecture, service entrance, main disconnect, voltage/amperage ratings, and distribution to building service panels.

One-Line Diagram of the electrical riser is not included in the plan set. Provide a complete one-line diagram showing the electrical service configuration including main service entrance, distribution panel(s), protective devices, branch circuits, and load distribution per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B. The diagram must clearly show how the service from Austin Energy connects to the customer's electrical system and distributes power throughout the development.

Provide One-Line Diagram of the electrical riser showing electrical service configuration, voltage, phases, main breaker, load calculations, and service routing strategy per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B. This is a required plan sheet for all sites.

Secondary riser configuration is not shown on plans, or one-line diagram of electrical riser is not provided. Please provide a one-line electrical riser diagram showing the distribution of service from the main service entrance through the secondary system to all buildings and units, drawn to standard electrical schematic conventions.

Secondary riser configuration not shown on plans and no one-line diagram of electrical riser provided. One-line riser diagram must be included on electrical plans showing secondary service distribution to all buildings and units.

comments.title: Electrical Disconnects Not Shown or Labeled on Electrical Plans
comments.comment: No electrical disconnects are shown or labeled on any electrical plan sheet in the submittal.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires disconnects to be shown and labeled on electrical plans for all sites. Sheet 21, the only electrical design sheet provided, is a site-level plan-view showing transformer locations, pull boxes, and underground routing — it contains no depiction of main service disconnects, transformer disconnects, or building-level disconnects. No building-level electrical floor plans showing service entrance equipment or disconnect locations are included in the 39-sheet plan set.
comments.applicableArea: Building electrical systems – main service disconnects for all 8 buildings
comments.resolution: Provide electrical plan sheets showing the location of main service disconnect(s) for each building, clearly labeled with amperage rating and voltage. Show the physical relationship between outdoor transformer/meter locations and indoor disconnect locations, including routing of service conductors. If building-level electrical plans are not within the scope of this site plan submittal, provide a written clarification and identify which submittal will include disconnect documentation.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Medium confidence (2/3 runs) — run-1 flagged this as unclear, noting that building-level architectural electrical plans may not be required at the site plan stage; reviewer should confirm the required scope of electrical documentation for this submittal.

perRunFindings.comment: Cannot fully verify from available evidence whether disconnects are shown and labeled on architectural electrical plans, as detailed electrical plans for individual buildings do not appear to be included in this preliminary site plan submission. If architectural electrical plans are required for this project, please provide them showing main service disconnects, transformer disconnects, and building-level disconnects clearly labeled and sized.
applicableAreas: Electrical plans and service entrance details

perRunFindings.comment: Disconnects not shown and labeled on electrical plans. Provide electrical plans showing the location of main service disconnect(s) for each building clearly labeled with amperage rating and voltage. Show the relationship between outdoor transformers/meters and indoor disconnect locations with routing information.

comments.title: Electrical Facility Legend Missing Proposed Facility Symbols and Inconsistent with Plans
comments.comment: The legend on Sheet 3 contains only existing electrical facility symbols and does not define proposed facility symbols, while Sheet 21 uses text callouts rather than legend-defined symbols — creating inconsistency between the legend and the plans.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires that electric facility symbols be identified in the legend and that legend symbols match those actually used in the plans. Two related deficiencies are present:
- Sheet 3 legend (Block 6) defines symbols only for existing electric facilities (Existing Power Pole & Down Guy, Existing Electric Meter, Existing Transformer Pad, Existing Overhead Electric Line, Existing Light Pole) — no symbols are defined for proposed facilities (proposed transformer pads, proposed pull boxes, proposed meters, proposed underground lines)
- Sheet 21 uses text callouts ('Electrical Transformer Pad,' 'Electrical Pull Box,' 'Electrical Meters,' 'Underground Electric Line') rather than graphical symbols defined in the legend, and Sheet 21 contains no local legend or cross-reference directing readers to Sheet 3 for symbol definitions
comments.sheets: General Notes (Sheet 3); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Site Plan – All Utilities (Sheet 9)
comments.applicableArea: All sheets showing electric facilities – legend on Sheet 3, plan graphics on Sheets 9, 19, and 21
comments.resolution: Add a complete set of proposed electric facility symbols to the Sheet 3 legend, including proposed transformer pad, proposed pull box, proposed electric meter, and proposed underground electric line (–E–). Standardize all electrical plans to use these defined symbols consistently, or alternatively add an explicit cross-reference note on Sheet 21 directing readers to Sheet 3 for symbol definitions and ensure the callouts used match the legend entries. Verify that symbols used on Sheets 9 and 19 are also consistent with the updated legend.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Medium confidence (2/3 runs); run-2 observed that Sheet 19 includes a legend entry for 'Transformer Pad (T symbol)' and 'E | Proposed Underground Electric' — reviewer should verify whether Sheet 19's legend partially addresses the deficiency.

perRunFindings.comment: Electric facility symbols are not identified in legend or symbols for proposed electric facilities are missing from the legend. Please provide legend entries for all proposed electric facilities shown on the plans (proposed transformers, proposed pull boxes, proposed meters, proposed underground lines, proposed service connections, and other relevant symbols).

Electric facility symbols not identified in legend on electrical plan sheet. Legend defining all electric facility symbols must be present on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) or have an explicit cross-reference note directing users to the legend location.
applicableAreas: Cover sheet or general notes sheet with legend

perRunFindings.comment: Legend symbols do not match symbols actually used in plans. Please ensure that all symbols used on site plan, utility plan, electrical plan, grading plan, and landscape plan exactly match the symbols shown in the legend, or add legend entries for any symbols used that are not currently in the legend.

Legend symbols do not clearly match symbols actually used in plans. Clarify legend consistency: either standardize on use of legend symbols (e.g., 'T' symbol, '--- OHE ---' notation) on all plans, or provide alternative legend defining text callouts used (e.g., "Electrical Transformer Pad," "Electrical Pull Box"). Ensure consistent symbol and label use across all sheets.

comments.title: CAD File Technical Requirements Cannot Be Verified from Submitted PDFs
comments.comment: CAD file compliance with Austin Energy's coordinate system, layer naming, color, and model space requirements cannot be verified because only PDF plan sheets were reviewed — the underlying DWG/DXF files are not available.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.4.2.6 and Table 1.4.3.A require AutoCAD files to meet the following technical specifications, none of which can be confirmed from the PDF plan sheets alone:
- Georeferenced to NAD 83 Texas Central Zone 4203 coordinate system
- All electric facilities placed on specified named layers with Magenta color: underground lines on 'Elec. UG', overhead lines on 'Elec. OH', poles on 'Elec. Pole', underground transformers on 'Elec. Transf. UG', overhead transformers on 'Elec. Transf. OH', manholes on 'Elec. MH'
- All required objects in model space with UCS set to 'World'
The printed plan sheets show electric facilities in blue — inconsistent with the required Magenta specification — though this may be a printing/display artifact rather than evidence of non-compliance. Sheet 21 identifies a source DWG file path ('P:\01_PROJECTS\AUSTIN\2023\2023-010-00 VALLEY VIEW TOWNHOMES\04_CAD\02_SHEETS\UTILITY ELEC PLAN.dwg, 2/28/2024, Chris_Rodgers') confirming a CAD file exists, but no coordinate system documentation is included.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) – CAD file path shown on sheet
comments.applicableArea: CAD files for all electrical design sheets
comments.resolution: Submit the native AutoCAD DWG or DXF files (version 2016 or newer) for technical review, or provide a written certification from the engineer of record confirming: (1) all files are georeferenced to NAD 83 Texas Central Zone 4203, (2) all electric facilities are placed on the required named layers (Elec. UG, Elec. OH, Elec. Pole, Elec. Transf. UG, Elec. Transf. OH, Elec. MH) with Magenta color, and (3) all required objects are in model space with UCS set to 'World'.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Status is 'unclear' because all runs agreed compliance cannot be verified from PDF review alone — reviewer should determine the correct mechanism for CAD file submission and verification for this project.

perRunFindings.comment: Cannot verify from available evidence whether CAD files are georeferenced with NAD 83 Texas Central Zone 4203. Please provide the AutoCAD CAD files (DWG or DXF format, version 2016 or newer) with certification that they are properly georeferenced to NAD 83 Texas Central Zone 4203 as required by UCM § 1.4.2.6.

CAD file georeferencing cannot be verified from plan sheets. CAD files must be verified to be georeferenced with NAD 83 Texas Central Zone 4203 coordinate system with all electric facilities in model space and UCS set to 'World'.

Cannot verify from available evidence whether electric facilities are placed on correct CAD layers (Elec. UG, Elec. OH, Elec. MH, Elec. Transf. OH, Elec. Transf. UG, Elec. Pole) with Magenta color per layer standards. Please provide the AutoCAD files for verification, or submit a certified list documenting the layer names and colors used for all electric facility objects.

Cannot definitively verify correct CAD layer assignment and Magenta color specification from printed sheets. CAD files must be verified to contain electric facilities on correct layers (Elec. UG, Elec. OH, Elec. MH, Elec. Transf. OH, Elec. Transf. UG, Elec. Pole) with Magenta color as specified in UCM § 1.4.2.6.

Cannot verify from available evidence whether required electric facility objects are in model space or UCS is set to 'World' per UCM § 1.4.2.6 requirements. Please provide the AutoCAD files for technical verification, or submit documentation certifying that all electric facility objects are placed in model space with UCS setting set to 'World'.
applicableAreas: CAD file model space and UCS settings

perRunFindings.comment: Cannot verify model space and UCS settings from printed sheets. CAD files must be verified to have all required objects in model space with UCS setting to 'World' per UCM § 1.4.2.6.

CAD file georeferencing to NAD 83 Texas Central Zone 4203 cannot be verified from available site plan image/PDF files. Provide the original AutoCAD (.dwg) files or a written certification from the engineer confirming that all CAD files are properly georeferenced to NAD 83 Texas Central Zone 4203 coordinate system per UCM § 1.4.2.6.

Cannot verify CAD file georeferencing from available evidence. Provide certification that the CAD file is georeferenced to NAD 83 Texas Central Zone 4203 per UCM § 1.4.2.6, and verify that all electric infrastructure elements are assigned to required Magenta layers (Elec. UG, Elec. OH, Elec. Pole, Elec. Transf. UG, Elec. Transf. OH, Elec. MH) per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.A.

comments.title: Utility Poles and Service Drops Not Labeled on Landscape Plan
comments.comment: Specific utility pole locations and service drop routing are not clearly shown or labeled on the Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) as required for all required utility plan sheets.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires poles and service drops to be shown on all required plan sheets, including the landscape plan. Sheet 31 shows an overhead electric (OHE) line along the southern boundary but provides no distinct pole symbols, pole labels, or service drop routing to buildings — a reviewer cannot identify individual pole locations or confirm clearances to structures or vegetation from this sheet. Sheet 9 similarly lacks labeled pole locations. Sheet 21 documents pull boxes and underground routing but does not explicitly mark the existing utility poles associated with the OHE line on the southern boundary.
comments.sheets: Site Plan – All Utilities (Sheet 9); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: Southern boundary overhead electric line corridor; western boundary OHE infrastructure; internal pull box locations
comments.resolution: Add clearly labeled utility pole symbols to Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) and Sheet 9 (Site Plan) showing all existing and proposed pole locations along the overhead electric lines on the site boundaries. Include service drop routing from poles to any service connection points. Ensure pull box locations shown on Sheet 21 are also depicted on Sheet 9.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Medium confidence (2/3 runs) — run-1 noted that Sheet 31 may show pole locations via cross-mark symbols along the OHE line but without explicit labels; reviewer should verify whether unlabeled symbols satisfy the 'clearly shown' requirement.

perRunFindings.comment: Poles or service drops are not clearly shown and labeled on the required plan sheets. While pull boxes are shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), utility poles along existing overhead electric lines are not explicitly marked on the Site Plan (Sheet 9) or Landscape Plan (Sheet 31). All poles and service drop infrastructure must be clearly identified on the site plan showing all utilities and landscape plan per UCM § 1.4.2.6.

Poles and service drops are not clearly shown on Landscape Plan (Sheet 31). Add pole locations and service drop routing to this sheet to demonstrate coordination with site grading, landscaping, and building placement. Show specific utility pole locations and how overhead or underground service is routed to serve the development.

comments.title: Service Type Not Clearly Designated on Site Plan and Landscape Plan
comments.comment: The overall electric service type (overhead, underground, or mixed) is not clearly designated on the Site Plan (Sheet 9) or Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), leaving a reviewer unable to determine service type from these sheets without cross-referencing Sheet 21.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires service type to be clearly designated on all required plan sheets. Sheet 21 clearly designates underground service through explicit 'Underground Electric Line' labels and pull box locations, but Sheets 9 and 31 show both existing overhead electric (OHE) lines on the boundaries and a proposed transformer pad without clarifying whether the development is served by overhead, underground, or a hybrid arrangement. The ambiguity prevents independent confirmation of service type from the utility and landscape plan sheets.
comments.sheets: Site Plan – All Utilities (Sheet 9); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: Entire site – electric service type designation
comments.resolution: Add a note on Sheet 9 and Sheet 31 explicitly stating the proposed service type (e.g., 'Proposed Service: Underground Electric Distribution' or 'New service: underground from Valley View Road connection to on-site transformer pads'). Clarify on both sheets that existing OHE lines along the boundaries are existing utilities remaining in place, distinct from the proposed underground distribution serving the development.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — verify whether service type designation is adequately conveyed by existing OHE and underground labels on Sheets 9 and 31, or whether an explicit note is required.

perRunFindings.comment: Service type (overhead or underground) is not clearly designated on Site Plan (Sheet 9) or Landscape Plan (Sheet 31). Add a clear note or legend entry on each required plan sheet stating the service type (e.g., 'Proposed Service: Underground Electric Distribution' or similar) to eliminate ambiguity and ensure all required sheets clearly identify whether the development uses overhead, underground, or mixed service type.

comments.title: Utility Plan Provides Insufficient Detail for Electric Facilities
comments.comment: The Utility Tap Plan (Sheet 19) does not provide adequate detail or documentation for proposed electric utilities, which are shown only as a generic line with no specifications.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires that the utility plan be provided at adequate scale with sufficient detail for all utilities shown. Sheet 19 is designed primarily as a water/wastewater tap plan and gives detailed labeling, DFU calculations, and profiles for those systems — but electric utility documentation is limited to a single generic '–E–' (Proposed Underground Electric) designation with no routing specifications, no detail, and no profile. No profile view of electric utilities is provided (profiles on Sheet 19 address water only). The electrical legend entry exists but the lines are not drawn on the plan, and no separate electrically-focused utility documentation is provided to compensate.
comments.applicableArea: Utility Tap Plan – proposed underground electric routing
comments.resolution: Either enhance Sheet 19 to include detailed underground electric routing with routing specifications and labeling adequate to distinguish electric lines from water/wastewater infrastructure, or provide a separate utility plan sheet focused on electric infrastructure at 1"=20' scale with complete routing, conduit paths, and connection details. At minimum, draw the '–E–' underground electric lines on Sheet 19 that are currently defined in the legend but not depicted.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — verify whether the level of electric detail on Sheet 19 meets UCM § 1.4.2.6 requirements given that Sheet 21 provides detailed electrical routing at the same scale.

perRunFindings.comment: Utility plan scale or layout may not be adequate for clear display of electric utilities. If electric utilities are shown on the utility plan, they must be at sufficient scale with adequate labeling and detail to distinguish from other utilities and allow clear review.
